coverage.formula: (cash today + money in over days 0..89) / money out over them = (¥400,000.00 + ¥1,260,000.00 + ¥0.00 funding landing) / ¥650,000.00; the conservative projection's own events (unconfirmed inflows not counted)

liquidity.formula: current ratio = (cash + receivables + inventory + other current assets) / (trade payables + other current liabilities + debt due within 12 months); quick ratio = (cash + receivables) / the same liabilities; committed capex payments are shown beside, not counted as a liability

summary: Cash falls below your ¥300,000.00 minimum on day 12 (¥60,000.00); the lowest point is −¥105,000.00 on day 30. A committed funding plan covers it for ¥3,113.93. Over the next 90 days, cash on hand and what comes in covers what goes out: 2.55× (¥1,660,000.00 against ¥650,000.00). Worst projected DSCR 2.00× (minimum 1.25×) and leverage 1.35× (maximum 2.50×): room for ¥27,000.00 more debt service a month and ¥1,245,000.00 more debt.
assumptions: Cash is read on the conservative projection of current books (the stored books plus live agreements), the same as Home: unconfirmed inflows are not counted and uncommitted facilities count as zero.

The 90-day cash coverage ratio is a reading of the projection's own cash in and out; it is not a balance-sheet current ratio. The current and quick ratios use your own entries for what the books do not hold.

Covenant room is read on the worst projected month of the mandate's horizon; a facility's capacity is what DSCR, leverage and its limit allow, not cash available, and it ignores the timing of when cash is needed (the capex screen tests that day by day).
Each facility's capacity is read on its own: the facilities share one DSCR and leverage room, so borrowing on one leaves less for the others.
Debt due within twelve months counts every payment in the next 365 days.
